references.text: The Gibeonites came to the Israelites and pretended to be from a distant land, which led to the covenant mentioned in verse 16.
Joshua made peace with them and entered into a covenant to let them live, just before they discovered the truth three days later.
The continuation of the story where the Israelites went out, came to the Gibeonite cities, and discovered that they were neighbors.
The Mosaic law on how the Israelites should treat cities far away versus those nearby, which the Gibeonites exploited by pretending to come from a distant land.
The prohibition against making covenants with the inhabitants of Canaan and their gods, which the Israelites broke in the case of the Gibeonites.
The command to devote the Canaanites to destruction and not make covenants with them, which stands in contrast to the covenant made with the Gibeonites.
